record.tranche_reason: The study measures whether sampled SAE features decompose into prompted sub-components and reports heterogeneous results, including clean decomposition and narrower-than-described activation patterns. This challenges the idea that SAE features are necessarily complete, atomic units, though it does not assess their stability or canonicality.
record.gate_note: The reported activation and decomposition outcomes are included. The arbitrary choice of layer 20 is not a result, and the cited meta-SAE work is not this study's result. The visualization link is not itself a reported result.
record.test_reason: The post checks whether Gemma Scope layer-20 features fire on ChatGPT-written phrases for guessed sub-concepts of each feature's Neuronpedia label. That measures how well the labels match activation behaviour, a related but different construct. It does not measure whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units (V5). A feature firing on all guessed sub-components does not show it splits into smaller latents, and the prompting failures are confounded by prompt quality. No version is tested; the finding goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The author concludes that SAE features are often less decomposable than their descriptions imply. Many decompose intuitively, while others fire on narrower subsets or could not be activated by the method. The author cautions that prompting may miss true feature behaviour and that more features are needed.
record.recipe_differences: Uses prompted sub-components and generated phrases to test Gemma Scope SAE feature activations, rather than the toy-network setup and measurements of the original superposition work.
record.method_sensitivity: The author says prompt formulation can affect whether a feature activates; describing a pattern instead of generating the relevant character pattern may cause failures. Layer 20 was chosen somewhat arbitrarily, but no outcome comparison across layers is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: For an unstated number of randomly sampled Gemma Scope layer-20 features, about 35% fired on phrases for all guessed sub-components of their label. Others fired on narrower subsets of their description. About a third could not be activated by the automated prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Auto-generated SAE feature descriptions often misstate the range of inputs that activate the feature (description fidelity).

record.problems: The number of sampled features is not stated. There are no reported controls or uncertainty estimates. The author says the automated prompts may fail to capture true feature behavior and that a larger feature sample is needed. The feature 6772 text and its linked URL have mismatched identifiers.

untested.parts: Completeness, stability across SAE runs or sizes, canonicality and atomicity of SAE features are not measured. Only label-to-activation agreement is measured.

record.verdict_notes: Informal LessWrong post with no controls, no uncertainty and no stated sample size. The meta-SAE work it cites is not this study's result. The reader's T5 'challenges' verdict on V5 overreads label-fidelity results as evidence on whether features are atomic.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transition, and regular geometry are not tested.
The study does not test capacity competition, dedicated dimensions, or polysemantic neurons.
The study does not test polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity.
The study does not measure feature distribution across neurons or test whether an SAE dictionary recovers sparse features.
It examines prompted decomposability and activation patterns, not feature stability across settings or whether features are canonical units.
The study does not test whether features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 2B, Gemma Scope SAE
rows.operation_detail: Measured the original SAE feature's activation on generated activating phrases for proposed sub-components.

conditions.value: 15 per feature: 3 for each of 5 ChatGPT-generated sub-components

rows.measure: Share of analyzed features that activated across all generated sub-components
rows.note: The reported clean decomposition across generated sub-components is contrary to features being complete, indivisible units. The number of features analyzed is not stated.
rows.check: Firing on all five generated sub-components shows the label matches broad activation. It does not show the feature splits into smaller units, so 'reversed' against V5 is unsupported. The number of features analysed is not stated and there is no baseline.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 2B, Gemma Scope SAE
rows.operation_detail: Measured feature activation on generated activating phrases for proposed sub-components.

conditions.value: 15 per feature: 3 for each of 5 ChatGPT-generated sub-components

rows.value: Around a third of features consistently failed to produce nonzero activations
rows.note: The author attributes many failures to prompts describing a pattern rather than producing the pattern itself, so this result does not establish that the features are incomplete or non-canonical.
rows.check: The author attributes most failures to prompts describing a pattern rather than producing it. This is a method failure, not evidence about feature units.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 2B, Gemma Scope SAE feature 6772
rows.operation_detail: Measured feature activation on generated phrases for proposed sub-components.
rows.measure: Activation pattern relative to the feature's broad description
rows.value: The feature tended to activate mostly on war-related inputs, especially German occupation during World War 2, despite a broader description concerning historical and political context in Denmark
rows.note: The text identifies feature 6772, but the linked Neuronpedia URL ends in 6722.
rows.check: Narrower activation than the Neuronpedia description is a mismatch between label and behaviour, not a test of completeness or canonicality. The ID is 6772 in the text but 6722 in the URL.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 2B, Gemma Scope SAE feature 2779
rows.operation_detail: Tested activation on phrases concerning concepts related to the feature's label.
rows.measure: Feature activation on seemingly related concepts
rows.value: Did not activate on the tested seemingly related concepts; top activations looked unrelated
rows.note: The author describes this feature as still mysterious and notes that the prompting technique may fail to capture true feature behavior.
rows.check: A single anecdotal label mismatch, which the author calls 'somewhat mysterious'. It does not bear on any version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Features reported as cleanly decomposable and feature 6772
reader_labels.reason: Some sampled features activated across generated sub-components, and feature 6772 showed a narrower activation pattern than its broad description; these results challenge treating SAE features as necessarily complete, indivisible units. Rows r1 and r3.
